transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in today because... I just keep beating myself up lately. I've been having this feeling that I'm not really senior material at my job. It's like I somehow fooled everyone into thinking I could handle way more than I actually can, and... I don't know, it's just really weighing on me.
Have you always tended to doubt yourself and feel like you're not good enough, or is this feeling of being a fraud at work something that's relatively new for you?

Well, I wouldn't say I've always been like this. I used to feel pretty okay about my work. But... looking back, these low, guilty periods have been hanging around off and on for about eleven months now. So it's not brand new, but it hasn't been my whole life either.
During these eleven months, have there been times when your mood and energy felt noticeably better, or has the low mood been pretty constant throughout?

Well, it hasn't just been low the entire time. Um, the noticeable up-and-down pattern really started about a month ago. That was right after I was asked to cover the senior analyst duties at work. So, yeah, lately it's been more back and forth instead of just constant.

During those times when your mood was better over the past month, did you notice that you needed less sleep than usual, or that you had a lot more energy and felt like you could do more things than normal?

Yeah, the sleep thing definitely happened. For a while there, I was sleeping maybe three or four hours a night, and... I'd still get up feeling completely ready to tackle the day. That is definitely not normal for me. Usually I need a lot more rest than that.

During those times when you were sleeping only three or four hours but still feeling energized, did you find yourself taking on a lot of new projects or goals at work or in your personal life—things that seemed like great ideas at the time but maybe were more than you'd normally attempt?

Yeah, I actually did. Um, I started taking on extra monitoring reports at work. And I would just start messaging clients and coworkers with all these ideas before anyone even asked me for them. It was... well, it was like I was trying to prove I could run the whole thing myself.

Before this past month when things started going up and down, during those first ten months or so, was there a time when your mood felt pretty normal and stable—not depressed, just kind of baseline—or was the low mood pretty much there the whole time?

No, not really. Looking back at those first ten months... the low mood was pretty much there the whole time. I don't remember having any stretches where I felt normal or back to my baseline. It was just a constant low until this past month.

During those times over the past month when you were sleeping only a few hours but feeling energized, did you also notice that your thoughts were racing, or that you were talking more than usual, or that you felt unusually confident or powerful?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I had a lot of ideas for work, like I said, but my mind wasn't really... racing. And I don't think I was talking more than normal, either. I definitely didn't feel powerful or anything like that. Just... awake and focused, I guess.
When you were sleeping only three or four hours a night and felt energized over the past month, how many days in a row would that typically last before your mood would dip back down again?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I didn't really keep track of the exact number of days. Um... it felt like maybe a few days at a time? But I couldn't give you a specific number before it would just drop off again.

When you think back to those times over the past month when you were sleeping only a few hours and feeling energized and focused, can you remember the longest stretch of days that lasted before your mood dropped back down? Was it at least four days in a row, or was it shorter than that?

I really couldn't say for sure if it was four days in a row. Like I said, I wasn't really keeping track. It might have been a few days, but I honestly don't know if it was exactly four days or more before the crash happened. I just remember the feeling, not really the timeline.

Over this past month when your mood has been going up and down, on those days when you were sleeping only three or four hours and feeling energized—did you feel like you actually needed less sleep than usual, or did you just happen to sleep less but still feel tired or like you needed more rest?

I definitely felt like I needed less sleep. It wasn't like I was tossing and turning and wishing I could sleep more. For a while there, I was sleeping maybe three or four hours and still getting up feeling completely energized and ready to tackle the day. That's really not normal for me, usually I need a solid eight hours to function, but during those stretches, I just didn't need it.

When you think about those stretches over the past month when you were sleeping just a few hours but feeling energized and focused, do you remember if any of those periods lasted for four days or longer before your mood dropped back down?

I know we kind of touched on this a minute ago, but... I really just don't have a solid answer for you on the exact number of days. It all just sort of blurs together when I look back at the month. 

I know you're looking to see if it hit that four-day mark, but since I wasn't marking it down on a calendar or anything, I really can't say for certain. It could have been four days, or maybe just two or three. I just know the energized feeling lasted for a bit before I crashed again.

During this past month, when you were sleeping just a few hours and feeling energized and focused, did you have at least one stretch where that feeling lasted for a full week or longer before your mood crashed?

No, definitely not a full week. Like I said, I'm not totally sure on the exact number of days, but I know for a fact it was never a whole week straight. It was shorter bursts than that before I'd crash again.

During those stretches over the past month when you were sleeping just a few hours and feeling energized, what's the longest number of days in a row that you can recall feeling that way before your mood dropped back down—would you say it was around 2-3 days, or closer to 4-5 days?

I really couldn't say for sure if it was closer to two to three days or four to five days. Like I mentioned, I wasn't really keeping track of it at the time. I just know it was a few days here and there, but pinning down the exact longest stretch... I just don't know.

When you think back to those energized stretches over the past month, if you had to compare them to something concrete—like a typical work week—would you say the longest one lasted about as long as a work week, or was it noticeably shorter than that?

Like I said before, it definitely wasn't a full week. So yeah, noticeably shorter than a work week. I just... I can't give you an exact number of days. It was just a few days at a time before I crashed.

During those stretches over the past month when you were sleeping just a few hours and feeling energized, do you remember if any of them lasted for at least 3 or 4 days in a row, or were they all shorter than that—like just 1 or 2 days?

I honestly don't know if it was three or four days, or just one or two. I mean, I really just wasn't paying that close attention to the exact number of days. I just know it was short bursts, but I can't break it down into those specific timeframes for you.

Let me try asking this a different way. During this past month when you felt energized on just a few hours of sleep, if you think about the longest stretch, would you say you felt that way for at least several days—like Monday through Thursday of a work week—or was it more like just a day or two?

I get that you're trying to pin down a specific timeframe here, but I just don't have one to give you. I really can't say if it was a Monday through Thursday kind of thing or just a day or two. 

Like I've been saying, I wasn't logging my days or keeping track of it like that. It was just short bursts of energy, and... that's really all I can tell you. I just don't have a clearer answer for you on the exact number of days.

When you think about this past month with those ups and downs, how many separate times would you say you had that energized feeling on just a few hours of sleep before crashing—was it maybe two or three times, or more like once a week or more often than that?

I honestly don't know the exact number of times, either. It all just kind of... blends together when I look back at the month. 

I know it happened more than once, but whether it was two or three times, or more than that, I really couldn't tell you. I just wasn't keeping a tally of how often it happened.

I understand you're not sure about exact days. Let me ask it this way: during this past month, do you remember at least one time when you felt energized on just a few hours of sleep for several days in a row—like, you'd wake up the next day still feeling that same energy and not needing more sleep, and that would continue for a few days before crashing?

I get what you're asking, but... I really just can't say for sure. I don't remember a specific time where I woke up day after day still running on that same energy. 

It might have happened that way, but I just don't have a clear memory of it lasting for a few days straight before a crash. Like I said, the whole month is just kind of a blur of those ups and downs, so I really can't confirm if it carried over like that.

Before these past eleven months started, did you have any stretches of time—weeks or months—where your mood felt pretty normal and stable, or has depression been a pretty consistent part of your life for longer than that?

I honestly don't really know. I haven't really thought about it like that before. I mean, I guess I've had normal times, but I couldn't tell you how long they lasted or when exactly they were. It's hard to remember what was going on before this past year.

I know you've mentioned the ups and downs over the past month, but let me ask you directly: do you think it's possible that one of those energized stretches lasted for four days or more in a row, even if you're not completely certain about it?

It's possible, yeah, but... I just really don't know. Like I said, the whole month is kind of a blur. I can't say for sure if any of those energized times lasted for four days straight. I just wasn't paying that close attention to the days.
